evidence.title: Understand What You Are Paying For - Carpet Area, Built-up or Super Built-up Area
evidence.property_name: Understand What You Are Paying For - Carpet Area, Built-up or Super Built-up Area
evidence.description: Area Type Calculation Area (Sq. Ft.) Effective Cost Per Sq. Ft. Carpet Area Net usable space within the walls. Includes living room, bedrooms, kitchen, and toilets. 1,000 INR 6,500 Built-up Area Carpet Area PLUS the area of inner and outer walls, and private balconies/terraces. 1,150 INR 5,652 Super Built-up Area Built-up Area PLUS a proportional share of common areas (lifts, lobby, stairs, club house). (Assuming a 30% Loading Factor) 1,300 INR 5,000 In this case, a buyer is paying INR 65,00,000 for a unit advertised at INR 5,000 per sq. ft. - based on Super Built-up Area. [...] Whereas, in reality, the space that is usable by a buyer, the actual area on which to lay carpets or live, is only 1,000 sq. ft. This means the true cost for the net usable space (Carpet Area) is INR 6,500 per square foot. The loading factor is 30% and represents the additional 300 sq. ft. that the buyer pays for to compensate for common amenities. This calculation shows why there is a need to always negotiate the price of the property on the Carpet Area as specified by RERA. ## What does a super built-up area include Built-up area of the flat Clubhouses Air Ducts Pipe/Shaft ducts Lifts Staircases Lobby Swimming pool Gymnasium Other Common Facilities ## Loading Factor [...] ## Pay only for what you buy As a buyer, always ask the builder about the carpeted square footage of the property and negotiate a price based on the square footage. When comparing different projects, always compare the price per square meter of carpeted area, not the built-up or square built-up area. This ensures that the comparison is accurate and that the prices quoted are valid and reasonable compared to prevailing prices in the area. Another important aspect is bank valuation when applying for a loan. The bank will send technical experts to inspect and evaluate the property. You can check if the carpet area provided by the builder is the same as what they rated. If there is a discrepancy, it should be pointed out to the client and the price renegotiated.

evidence.title: What is Carpet Area, Built up Area & Super Area
evidence.property_name: What is Carpet Area, Built up Area & Super Area
evidence.description: ## How to Calculate Carpet Area? Formula to calculate carpet area Carpet area = Area of bedroom + living room + balconies + toilets – the thickness of the inner walls Suggested Read: What RERA Carpet Area Means and How is it Calculated ## Important Things About Carpet Area When you go to buy a house and check the carpet area, you must keep the following things in mind:- A builder must include carpet area in marketing brochures, sale deeds and sale agreements. You must check the actual carpet area given and the carpet area promised; if there is a discrepancy, then you must ask for a refund of that amount [...] Take Clarifications You must clarify definitions and measurements of the carpet area, built-up area and super built-up area with developers or sellers. This ensures transparency and prevents misunderstandings. Assess Utility Figure out the use of the carpet area as per your personal preferences and lifestyle requirements since it impacts the property’s functionality. Evaluate Value Proposition Make a comparison of the properties as per their super built-up area to analyse the value proposition for shared facilities. Negotiate Well Negotiate the prices on the basis of the actual usable space of the carpet area and additional features of the super built-up area. This brings transparency to real estate transactions. [...] | Nullification of Unfair Agreements | Sale agreements that are not based on the carpet area for pricing can be treated as unfair trade practices. RERA authorities have the power to declare such agreements "null and void." |
